pivot: Whether any resulting evaluator arrangement carries revocation/publication authority sitting outside the regulated lab's own veto, versus remaining self-vetoed (lab can revoke, gag, or scope it at will) — regardless of whether the actor doing the binding is a state (E12) or a horizontal cross-lab pact (E10-to-E10)
pivot_observable: Text of any announced evaluator/oversight arrangement (Anthropic's or another lab's): does it name who selects the evaluator, who can revoke access, and whether findings publish without the regulated lab's consent
pivot_because: This is the one variable that reorders the outcome set rather than just shifting confidence inside it. If veto sits outside the lab, the situation is materially different — an artifact exists that could bind conduct, feed the resignation-pressure question, and give the public-backlash sentiment an institutional attachment point. If veto stays inside the lab, every flavor of motion (Amodei's proposal, a narrowed unilateral pilot, even a second lab joining) collapses into the same functional bucket: theatre-with-language, changing nothing structurally. attention-substrate's own r2 revision folds its E12-only framing into exactly this test ('any embedded-evaluator move... stays a self-vetoed pilot'), which is what promotes veto-locus over jurisdiction-source as the true hinge.
rival_pivots_rejected: E12 jurisdiction-assertion (attention-substrate r1): the brief already shows the E12 actor's response — Sacks's public attack and the Trump/Huang stage appearance — as hostile, so this variable is already resolved inside the brief rather than live; it's a background condition, not a hinge. E9-to-E10 sentiment conversion (ai-public-backlash r1): abandoned by the same minute in r2, which rewrote its own mechanism to E10-to-E12 — a claim that keeps its prediction while swapping its causal story isn't testing either mechanism. Second public resignation (pressure-model): this is a downstream indicator conditioned on the same binding/non-binding fact, not an independent variable — it moves with the pivot, doesn't reorder it. Preemption contest / federal-vs-patchwork framing (ai-us-policy-direction r1): conceded to attention-substrate's framing in r2, folded into the veto-locus question rather than standing apart from it. Whether a second frontier lab signs on (touched by attention-substrate, ai-public-backlash, ai-lab-revealed-priorities but argued by none): this is a magnitude question nested inside the veto-locus pivot, not a separate axis — a second lab signing something self-vetoed doesn't reorder anything, so it's absorbed rather than rival.
ruling: The load-bearing floor is E10-into-structure (institutional crystallization with externally-held veto) rather than E9 (sentiment) or E12 (state assertion) alone, because every minute's outcome collapses to the same non-binding bucket unless some arrangement — state-imposed or cross-lab — strips revocation/publication control from the regulated lab itself, and the minutes show no path to that by 2026-12-17.
because: Six of seven minutes converge on 'nothing binding by 2026-12-17,' but they converge for different stated reasons (sentiment-stall, state-absence, lab-reluctance) until ai-regulation-teeth names the actual operational test — who selects, who revokes, who can veto publication — and attention-substrate explicitly adopts that test in its r2 revision to distinguish a 'self-vetoed pilot' from real crystallization. ai-lab-revealed-priorities is the sole minute on the other side, arguing Anthropic will be forced into a concrete unilateral act, but even its own claim describes that act as unilateral and lab-controlled, i.e. it does not contest that veto stays internal — it only contests whether motion happens at all, which is a confidence shift, not a reorder.
threat_live: A self-vetoed pilot arrangement (scoped, time-boxed, lab-revocable) becomes newly likely on this branch, and its danger is that it functions as pressure-relief: it lets Anthropic appear responsive without ceding veto, which forecloses both the harder external-veto arrangement and the second high-stakes resignation that pressure-model's mechanism depends on. This risk arrives with the branch (a visible-but-hollow compensating act) rather than existing beforehand.
strongest_minute: ai-regulation-teeth — it is the only minute that operationalizes 'binding' into three checkable terms (selector, revocation, publication veto) instead of leaving the word to do unexamined work; the rest of the panel, including a rival on r2, absorbs its framing.
weakest_minute: ai-public-backlash — it kept its exact prediction from r1 to r2 while replacing its entire causal mechanism (E9-to-E10 sentiment-stall became E10-to-E12 institution-stall), which means the claim was never actually falsifiable by the mechanism it now claims to test.
shared_assumption: That Amodei's embedded-evaluator proposal is the sole vehicle through which 'binding' could occur — five of seven minutes frame the entire question as whether that specific proposal crystallizes, without arguing why a wholly separate mechanism (e.g., a state consent decree, an insurer-driven standard, or a multi-lab pact with no connection to Amodei's proposal) is out of scope.
smuggled_assumption: pressure-model imports interiority the brief did not grant: 'he modeled the cost (equity) as smaller than the stakes of silence' asserts Coxon's internal weighing, not an observable act — the question asks what future his public behavior implies, not what he believed while doing it.
unresolved: Whether a non-Amodei-shaped path to externally-held veto (state consent decree, insurance/liability standard, multilateral non-US instrument) is plausible within the window — no minute tests this because all frame the question through Amodei's proposal as the only live vehicle.
